problem: Diffusion navigation policies trained by pure imitation inherit sub-optimality and redundancy from expert demos and suffer covariate shift. They therefore need a costly 'generate-then-filter' pipeline with an auxiliary critic/selector and dense sampling at inference, which adds latency on edge devices.
motivation: Real-time deployment on embedded hardware requires fast, selector-free planning that stays robust in unseen scenes. RL fine-tuning of diffusion via BPTT is unstable and expensive, so the authors seek a simple way to concentrate the policy's output distribution on high-reward trajectories.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained diffusion navigation policy by sampling N trajectories from itself, keeping the top-k by reward, and imitating them with a softmax-reward-weighted denoising loss (REPS-style), so no selector is needed at inference.
insight: Self-imitation concentrates the trajectory distribution (intra-modal convergence). This lets the model drop the critic and use deterministic DDIM with few steps: at 3 steps NavDP SR collapses to 0.275 while SIDP keeps 0.655. Ablations show temperature tau=1.0 is best, goal-agnostic training improves SR/SPL and exploration area, and the curriculum prevents early-stage collapse. Synthetic DAgger hurts NavDP (causal confusion, forgetting), whereas self-generated corrections stay in-distribution.
method: Reward-guided self-imitation: sample N candidate trajectories from pi_theta online, score with a reward, keep the top-k, and fit them by supervised denoising, avoiding BPTT through the denoising chain.
Importance weights: REPS closed form p* ∝ pi exp(r/tau), with softmax over top-k rewards; the loss is the reward-weighted DDPM epsilon-prediction loss L_SIDP.
Reward: collision penalty (lambda 10, via ESDF query), step cost (0.5), geodesic progress (5), docking bonus within 0.5 m (10).
Goal-agnostic exploration: auxiliary goals sampled in ±60° and 3–5 m; the point goal is replaced by a goal-agnostic embedding with uniform weights, preserving multi-modality and regularizing.
Reward-driven curriculum: admit a scenario only if R_max >= tau_max (feasible) and R_range >= tau_range (informative), acting as a gated cold-start protector.
Training environment: reuse InternData-N1 RGB-D observations, generate new goals from the scene ESDF, and initialize from NavDP without the critic (AdamW, lr 2e-5, batch 128, 2xA100, ~35 h).
Efficient inference: no selector or critic; deterministic DDIM with 5 or 3 steps, single sample.

setting.backbone: NavDP diffusion policy (RGB-D encoder + diffusion transformer, critic removed), fine-tuned via self-imitation
setting.training_data: Initialized from NavDP pretrained on InternData-N1; self-imitation on self-generated trajectories with new goals over InternData-N1 scenes/observations (ESDF-based rewards, no expert labels)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus point goal relative to camera
setting.action_space: predicted relative waypoint sequence (H x 3) from diffusion, tracked by a controller
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (InternVLA-N1 S1 benchmark); ESDF-based training environment
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged ESDF/geodesic only for training rewards); real-world depth from stereo via BANet

numbers_note: Ablations (temperature, goal-agnostic, curriculum, DAgger, robustness curves) are only given in figures, so no numbers are extracted. The InternVLA-N1 S1 benchmark is not a canonical name, so it is recorded as other; the split is labelled test as the benchmark is evaluation-only. The 'val' split for the ablation subset is a guess.
results: On InternVLA-N1 S1, SIDP reaches mSR 79.11 / mSPL 72.72, versus NavDP 73.22 / 70.95, with the largest gain on InternScenes-Commercial (SR 81.19 vs 71.25). On Jetson Orin Nano it is 2.48x faster with 5-step DDIM (110 ms vs 273 ms) and higher SR (0.674 vs 0.549). Real-world mSR is 90.25 vs 83.25 for NavDP.
limitations: Rewards and training rely on ESDF/geodesic information from InternData-N1 scenes, not real-world interaction; training reuses recorded observations rather than a full simulator.
Evaluated only on point-goal navigation with a single benchmark family and a NavDP baseline. Ablations are small (5 scenes, 500 trials) and shown only in figures.
Gains in SPL are modest (ClutteredEnv-Easy SPL is below NavDP).
